toxicity.notes: Bark latex mildly toxic in large amounts. Use under Ayurvedic practitioner supervision only.

Alstonia Scholaris.native_region: Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Southern China
Alstonia Scholaris.preparation: Bark decoction: boil 3g dried bark powder in 200ml water for 10 min, filter, drink once daily. Never self-medicate — consult practitioner.
Alstonia Scholaris.description: Saptaparni is one of the sacred trees of Ayurveda. Its name means 'seven-leaved' and it has been used for centuries in Indian traditional medicine for fever, respiratory ailments and skin conditions. Modern research confirms its antimalarial and antibacterial properties.
contraindications: Pregnancy
Children under 12
Self-medication strictly prohibited
High doses cause vomiting

toxicity.notes: Safe at recommended doses. Long-term use: monitor liver enzymes annually.

Arjun.native_region: Indian Subcontinent — riverbanks and moist deciduous forests
Arjun.preparation: Bark powder: 1-3g with warm milk or water twice daily on empty stomach. Arjunarishta (classical liquid formulation): 15-30ml with equal water after meals.
Arjun.description: Arjuna is Ayurveda's premier cardiac herb, documented in ancient texts for 3000 years. Multiple clinical trials confirm significant reduction in cardiac symptoms. It is the primary herb in classical Ayurvedic cardiology.
contraindications: Consult cardiologist if on anti-hypertensives or statins
Not a replacement for prescribed cardiac medication

toxicity.notes: Fruit and leaves are very safe for all age groups including children.

ayurvedic_uses: Irritable bowel syndrome and chronic diarrhoea
Digestive tonic — balances all three doshas
Bael.preparation: Dried fruit pulp powder: 5-10g with warm water before meals. Fresh fruit sherbet: blend pulp with water and jaggery. Leaf juice: 10-15ml twice daily for diabetes support.
Bael.description: Bael is one of the most sacred trees in Hinduism and one of the most effective digestive herbs in Ayurveda. The unripe fruit stops diarrhoea; the ripe fruit relieves constipation. This dual action is unique in plant medicine.
contraindications: Large amounts may cause constipation
Space 2 hours away from thyroid medications

toxicity.notes: Safe for all age groups. Avoid high medicinal doses during pregnancy.

Basil.native_region: Indian Subcontinent and Southeast Asia — cultivated worldwide
ayurvedic_uses: Stress and anxiety reduction — powerful adaptogen
Basil.preparation: Tea: boil 10 fresh leaves in 1 cup water for 5 min, add ginger and honey. Drink 2-3 cups daily. Chew 4-5 fresh leaves on empty stomach each morning. Juice: 10-15ml twice daily.
Basil.description: Tulsi is the most sacred plant in Hinduism and the most important adaptogenic herb in Ayurveda. Used for 5000+ years, it is called 'the queen of herbs.' Every part has medicinal value. Modern research confirms anti-viral, anti-bacterial, anti-diabetic and anti-cancer properties.
contraindications: Blood thinning medications (Warfarin)
Diabetes medications — monitor blood sugar
May reduce fertility with long-term very high doses

toxicity.notes: Leaf preparations safe. Avoid inhaling dried leaf dust — can irritate airways.

Chinar.native_region: Kashmir Valley, Iran, Eastern Mediterranean, Central Asia
Chinar.preparation: Leaf decoction: boil 10g fresh leaves in 400ml water, reduce by half, strain. Use as topical wash for skin conditions or drink 1 cup daily for systemic inflammation.
Chinar.description: Chinar is Kashmir's iconic sacred tree, revered for centuries in Sufi poetry and Kashmiri culture. Used in both Ayurvedic and Unani systems of medicine, its large leaves are a traditional remedy for inflammatory and skin conditions.
contraindications: Avoid inhaling powdered dry leaf
No known drug interactions at therapeutic doses

toxicity.notes: One of the safest medicinal plants. Safe for children, pregnant women, elderly.

Guava.preparation: Leaf tea: boil 8-10 fresh leaves in 1 litre water for 10 min. Drink 1 cup 2-3x daily before meals. Wound poultice: crush fresh leaves and apply directly.
Guava.description: Guava leaf is one of the world's most researched traditional diabetes remedies. A 2010 clinical trial in Japan showed guava leaf tea significantly reduces post-meal blood sugar spikes. The mechanism involves inhibition of alpha-glucosidase enzymes.
contraindications: Monitor blood sugar closely if on diabetes medication — synergistic effect
May cause pagination in very large amounts

toxicity.notes: All parts safe. Seeds are the most potent part — use in recommended dose only.

Jamun.native_region: Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia — grows near water sources
ayurvedic_uses: Diabetes treatment — converts starch to energy not sugar
Jamun.preparation: Seed powder: dry seeds, grind to fine powder. Take 1-2g with water twice daily 30 min before meals. Fresh fruit: eat 10-15 fruits daily in season. Bark decoction for mouth ulcers and gum disease.
Jamun.description: Jamun is perhaps the most powerful anti-diabetic plant in Ayurveda. The compound jamboline specifically inhibits the conversion of starch to sugar. Widely validated in modern pharmacological research, seed powder shows comparable effect to some oral hypoglycaemic drugs in studies.
contraindications: Do not combine with insulin without medical supervision — hypoglycemia risk
Avoid eating on empty stomach
Constipating in large amounts

toxicity.notes: ⚠ SEEDS ARE HIGHLY TOXIC — contain curcin (ricin-like toxin). External leaf application is safe. NEVER consume seeds, raw fruit or latex.

Jatropha.native_region: Tropical Americas — widely planted across India for biodiesel
ayurvedic_uses: External wound healing and antiseptic (leaf paste)
Toothache relief via latex applied externally
Jatropha.preparation: EXTERNAL USE ONLY. Fresh leaf paste: crush leaves and apply to wounds or inflamed joints 2x daily. Latex: apply tiny amount directly to tooth cavity with cotton. Never take internally without an expert Ayurvedic practitioner.
Jatropha.description: Jatropha has important external medicinal applications documented in tribal and Ayurvedic medicine. However, it is one of the few medicinal plants with genuinely dangerous toxicity if misused. Respect it for what it is — a powerful external medicine.
contraindications: NEVER eat seeds or fruit — potentially fatal
Keep away from children and animals
Never use internally without expert supervision
Latex causes eye inflammation — avoid contact

toxicity.notes: Completely safe. Among the safest medicinal plants in all traditions.

Lemon.native_region: Northeast India (Assam region) — cultivated globally for 2000+ years
ayurvedic_uses: Vitamin C and immune system activation
Lemon.preparation: Fresh juice: squeeze 1/2 lemon in 200ml warm water, drink on empty stomach each morning. Lemon peel tea: steep dried peel in hot water 5 min. Topical: dilute 1:3 with water for skin application.
Lemon.description: Lemon is a cornerstone of Ayurvedic dietary medicine (Ahara Chikitsa). Despite being acidic, it has an alkalizing effect in the body — a paradox documented in both Ayurveda and modern nutritional science. The peel contains the most potent compounds.
contraindications: Undiluted juice erodes tooth enamel — rinse mouth after
GERD: use cautiously, take with food
Space 2 hours from iron supplements — reduces absorption

toxicity.notes: Leaves and bark are safe. Raw mango sap and peel can irritate sensitive skin.

Mango.native_region: Indian Subcontinent — India is origin of all cultivated mango varieties
ayurvedic_uses: Anti-diabetic leaf tea — inhibits glucose absorption
Liver tonic and bile flow stimulation
Anaemia treatment (high iron in raw mango)
Mango.preparation: Leaf tea: soak 10-15 young leaves overnight in 400ml water, drink on empty stomach next morning. Bark decoction: 5g in 200ml water for dental hygiene. Dried mango powder (amchur): 1-2 tsp with meals for digestion.
Mango.description: India's national fruit has significant medicinal value in every part — leaf, bark, seed, flower and fruit. Mangiferin, unique to mango, has documented anti-diabetic, anti-viral and anti-cancer properties in clinical research. The leaf tea is one of India's oldest folk remedies for diabetes.
contraindications: Very ripe fruit: high glycaemic index — monitor if diabetic
Raw sap (latex): contact dermatitis in some people
Kidney disease: limit due to high potassium

toxicity.notes: Toxic to infants — never give neem oil or seeds internally to children under 2. Not for internal use during pregnancy. External topical use is safe for all ages.

ayurvedic_uses: Dental hygiene — neem twigs as toothbrush (proven effective)
Neem.preparation: Skin: grind fresh leaves to paste, apply topically, leave 20 min, rinse. Dental: chew twig end to expose fibres, use as toothbrush. Internal (adults only): 1-2g dried leaf powder with warm water, morning only, 4-week cycles.
Neem.description: Neem is called 'the village pharmacy' because every part has medicinal use. Over 140 bioactive compounds identified. It is one of the world's most researched medicinal plants with documented anti-bacterial, anti-fungal, anti-viral, anti-diabetic and anti-cancer properties.
contraindications: NEVER give to infants or children under 2
Not for internal use in pregnancy
Autoimmune conditions: may over-stimulate immunity
Organ transplant: do not use immunosuppressant interactions

toxicity.notes: All parts safe. Root bark in very large amounts may cause nausea. Fruit and peel completely safe.

Pomegranate.native_region: Persia (Iran) — cultivated in India for 3000+ years
ayurvedic_uses: Highest antioxidant capacity of any common fruit
Anti-inflammatory for arthritis and inflammatory bowel
Antibacterial for oral health (gum disease, bad breath)
Pomegranate.preparation: Fresh juice: 200ml daily on empty stomach. Peel powder: dry peel, grind fine, 2-3g with honey 2x daily for digestive issues. Peel decoction: boil 10g dried peel in 400ml water for mouthwash and gargle.
Pomegranate.description: Pomegranate is one of the most antioxidant-rich substances ever measured. Punicalagins, unique to pomegranate, are converted by gut bacteria to urolithin A — one of the most potent anti-ageing compounds discovered. Ayurveda used all parts for different conditions 3000 years before modern science confirmed the mechanisms.
contraindications: May inhibit CYP3A4 enzyme — space 2h from medications metabolised by this pathway
Blood pressure medications: additive effect — monitor
May lower blood sugar — monitor if diabetic

toxicity.notes: Seeds and oil mildly toxic if consumed. External skin use is safe and well-documented. Use under guidance for any internal application.

Pongamia Pinnata.native_region: Indian Subcontinent, Southeast Asia, Northern Australia — coastal and riparian forests
ayurvedic_uses: Chronic skin diseases: eczema, psoriasis, scabies (topical)
Pongamia Pinnata.preparation: Karanja oil (cold-pressed): apply to affected skin areas twice daily, massage gently. Fresh leaf paste: crush leaves, apply to wounds. Seed oil mixed with sesame oil (1:4) for sensitive skin.
Pongamia Pinnata.description: Karanja is an essential tree in Ayurvedic Dravyaguna (medicinal plant science) for skin conditions. Its oil is one of the main ingredients in classical formulations like Mahamarichyadi Oil. Modern dermatology research confirms significant anti-fungal and anti-bacterial efficacy.
contraindications: Do not consume seeds or seed oil internally
Patch test before large-area application
Avoid on broken or weeping wounds initially

toxicity.notes: Leaves and fruit are completely safe. Avoid apple seeds in large quantities.

Apple.preparation: Leaf tea: boil 3-5 dried leaves in water. Drink 1 cup daily for digestive irritation. Topical wash: use leaf decoction for minor skin scrapes.
Apple.description: While primarily known for its fruit, apple leaves have been used in traditional folk medicine for their cooling and astringent properties, particularly for soothing the digestive tract.
contraindications: No known contraindications for leaf tea in therapeutic doses

toxicity.notes: Leaves and silk are safe. Corn silk is the primary medicinal part used.

Corn.preparation: Corn Silk Tea: boil 2 tbsp dried corn silk in 2 cups water for 5 min. Drink 1-2 cups daily. Leaf decoction: used historically for urinary tract cooling.
Corn.description: In Ayurveda, corn silk is valued as a powerful diuretic that cleanses the urinary system. It is particularly effective for soothing inflammatory conditions of the bladder and kidneys.
contraindications: Low potassium levels (due to diuretic effect)
Severe kidney disease without medical supervision

toxicity.notes: Leaves are safe in moderate doses. Contain trace amounts of amygdalin (less than seeds).

Peach.preparation: Cold infusion: steep 1 tbsp dried leaves in cold water for 4 hours. Drink in small sips for nausea. Leaf syrup: traditionally used for children's coughs.
Peach.description: Peach leaves are a traditional demulcent and sedative used to calm the 'upper heat' in the body, particularly in the stomach and respiratory system.
contraindications: Pregnancy (due to trace amygdalin)
High doses may cause dizziness

toxicity.notes: Leaves are very safe and widely used in culinary traditions (e.g., Dolma).

Grape.native_region: Mediterranean region, Central Europe, Southwestern Asia
Grape.preparation: Leaf decoction: boil 10-15g dried leaves in water. Drink for circulatory health. Culinary: steamed/boiled leaves used as food wraps provide fiber and nutrients.
Grape.description: Draksha (Grape) is considered one of the 'best among fruits' in Ayurveda. The leaves share the fruit's cooling and blood-toning properties, particularly for venous health.
contraindications: Consult if on blood thinners due to high Vitamin K content

toxicity.notes: ⚠ LEAVES CONTAIN SOLANINE AND TOMATINE. Ingestion of large amounts can be dangerous. Only use externally in folk remedies.

Tomato.native_region: Western South America — global major crop
Tomato.preparation: EXTERNAL USE ONLY. Crush fresh leaves and rub on insect bites or stings. Never ingest tomato leaves or stems.
Tomato.description: While the fruit is a global staple, the tomato plant itself belongs to the nightshade family. The leaves contain alkaloids that are toxic if ingested but have served as folk remedies for external irritations for centuries.
contraindications: NEVER ingest internally
Keep away from children and pets
May cause contact dermatitis in sensitive individuals
